intro.title: Multiple State Variables
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that manages multiple independent pieces of reactive state. You will learn how to declare and use several separate ref() variables to track different data, like a user's name and age. The core concept is understanding how Vue's reactivity system can handle multiple state variables simultaneously within a single component. You will work with the ref() function from Vue's Composition API and bind these variables to different elements in the template. By the end, you'll have a functional app that updates and displays multiple data points independently.
intro.usecase: In real-world Vue applications, managing multiple state variables is essential for handling complex user interfaces. For example, in an e-commerce product page, you might need separate reactive variables for product details, user selections like size and color, quantity in cart, and inventory status—all updating independently as users interact. Dashboard interfaces commonly use multiple state variables to track different data sets, filter selections, and UI states like expanded panels or active tabs. This pattern allows developers to build responsive, modular components where each piece of state can be updated without affecting unrelated parts of the interface.
